title: Abbr Hint
summary: Turns jargon like TAT or SLA into a tappable, focusable hint so readers on touch screens and keyboards can see what it means.
description: Makes each abbreviation a dotted, tappable, keyboard-focusable hint instead of a hover-only <abbr title>, can spell it out on first use, exposes the expansion to screen readers, and flags terms missing from the glossary. The hint is portalled and flips to stay on screen.
catches: Abbreviations whose only explanation is a hover-only title attribute
First use of a term in a block of text, which can be spelled out inline
Abbreviations in the text that the glossary does not cover
limits: Matches whole words case-sensitively, so a differently cased spelling is not linked
Only knows the terms you put in the glossary; it does not guess expansions
a11y: Each term is a <button> with aria-expanded, reachable by Tab
The expansion is linked with aria-describedby, so screen readers hear it without opening the hint
stops: Readers guess at jargon like TAT
